title: Line Up for the Photo
statement:
A class of **n** students is lining up for a class photo. The photographer wants the shortest student on the left and the tallest on the right.

Given the heights of the students in centimetres, print them in **non-decreasing** order (from smallest to largest; equal heights may appear next to each other).
input:
The first line contains an integer **n**.

The second line contains n integers h[1], ..., h[n], the heights.
output: Print the n heights in non-decreasing order on one line, separated by spaces.
hints: Every language has a built-in sort: `sort(a.begin(), a.end())` in C++, `a.sort()` in Python, `Arrays.sort(a)` in Java.
In JavaScript remember to sort numbers with `a.sort((x, y) => x - y)`; the default sort compares text.
editorial:
Read the numbers into an array and sort it with the standard library sort, then print it. A simple O(n^2) sort like bubble sort is too slow for n = 10^5 in general, so learn to use the built-in one. Because heights are small (50 to 250) you could also use counting sort.

Complexity: O(n log n).
